install.fail2ban.description: Fail2ban scans system logs (e.g. SSH) and automatically bans IP addresses after too many failed login attempts. It protects against brute-force attacks without manual intervention. After installing, you'll be able to add your own rules (jails) in the Fail2ban tab.
install.mariadb.description: MariaDB is a database server. Choose the install source: the package from the default Alma/Rocky repository (older but proven version) or the official MariaDB.com repository (newer version, your choice). After installing, a random 16-character password is generated and set as the database root password, saved to /root/.mariadb.
install.mariadb.password_hint: The generated password (16 characters) is the main MariaDB root password, saved to /root/.mariadb on the server - read it over SSH.

install.mariadb.confirm_install: Install MariaDB? This may take a few minutes.

install.postgresql.description: PostgreSQL is a database server. Choose the install source: the package from the default Alma/Rocky repository (older version from the AppStream module) or the official PGDG repository (postgresql.org, newer version, your choice). After installing, the cluster is initialized (initdb) and a random 16-character password is generated and set as the postgres user's password, saved to /root/.postgresql.
install.postgresql.password_hint: The generated password (16 characters) is the main password for the postgres user, saved to /root/.postgresql on the server - read it over SSH.
install.postgresql.local_version_unknown: Couldn't determine the version - the package may not be available in this repository.
install.postgresql.mode_official_detail: Pick a specific version (16 or 17), the repository is added automatically.

postgresqlperf.title: Settings
postgresqlperf.description: Adjust key performance settings. Changes will restart the PostgreSQL service.
postgresqlperf.confirm_save: Save the new performance settings? The PostgreSQL service will be restarted.
install.mongodb.description: MongoDB is a document-oriented (NoSQL) database. Alma/Rocky don't have MongoDB in the default repositories (SSPL license), so installation is only available from the official MongoDB Inc. repository. After installing, a random 16-character password is generated, set as the database admin password, and authorization is enabled - the password is saved to /root/.adminmongodb.
install.mongodb.no_local_repo_note: No local Alma/Rocky repository version - MongoDB isn't available there.
install.mongodb.setup_incomplete_note: The MongoDB package is installed, but password/authorization setup was not completed (e.g. an earlier run was interrupted) - the database is currently reachable WITHOUT a password. Pick a version and run it again to finish setup.
install.mongodb.password_hint: The generated password (16 characters) is the MongoDB admin password (user "admin"), saved to /root/.adminmongodb on the server - read it over SSH.
install.mongodb.confirm_install: Install MongoDB? This may take a few minutes.

mongodbperf.description: Adjust key performance settings. Changes will restart the MongoDB service.
mongodbperf.max_connections_hint: MongoDB default: 65536 - lower it on small servers
mongodbperf.profiler_hint: Enabling logs slow queries, at the cost of a small performance overhead
mongodbperf.confirm_save: Save the new performance settings? The MongoDB service will be restarted.
install.redis.description: Redis is a fast in-memory key-value database (cache, queues, sessions). Choose the install source: the package from the default Alma/Rocky repository (AppStream module) or the official Redis Ltd repository (packages.redis.io, always the latest version). After installing, a random 16-character password is generated and set as the access password (requirepass), saved to /root/.redispw.
install.redis.password_hint: The generated password (16 characters) is the Redis access password (requirepass), saved to /root/.redispw on the server - read it over SSH.
install.redis.local_version_unknown: Couldn't determine the version - the package may not be available in this repository.
install.redis.mode_official_detail: Always the latest version from packages.redis.io - no specific version choice (Redis Ltd doesn't maintain separate per-version repositories).
install.redis.confirm_install: Install Redis? This may take a few minutes.
install.redis.setup_incomplete_note: The Redis package is installed, but the access password was not set (e.g. an earlier run was interrupted) - the database is currently reachable WITHOUT a password. Pick a source and run it again to finish setup.
redisperf.title: Settings
redisperf.description: Adjust key performance settings. Changes are applied immediately, without restarting the Redis service.
redisperf.slowlog_hint: Enabling logs queries slower than 10ms, at the cost of a small performance overhead
redisperf.save_success: Saved and applied immediately, no Redis restart needed.
redisperf.confirm_save: Save the new performance settings? They'll be applied immediately, without restarting the Redis service.
install.php-fpm.description: PHP-FPM via Remi, multiple versions side by side (each its own systemd service, e.g. php85-php-fpm). Pick one version to install - once installed it appears as its own manageable service below; you can come back here later to add more versions.
install.php-fpm.no_versions: No PHP versions available - check that the Remi repository is reachable.
install.frankenphp.description: FrankenPHP is a PHP application server built on Caddy, paired with a Thread-Safe (ZTS) PHP build via a separate repository (static-php) - independent from the PHP-FPM (Remi) versions above, which stay untouched. Pick a ZTS stream to install. The systemd service is NOT started automatically after install - test it standalone first (frankenphp php-server) before wiring it behind your existing Caddy, since FrankenPHP can itself act as a web server on the same ports.
install.frankenphp.no_versions: No PHP-ZTS streams available - check that the static-php repository is reachable.
install.frankenphp.confirm_install: Install FrankenPHP + PHP {version} ZTS? This may take a few minutes.
install.frankenphp.installed_hint: The frankenphp.service systemd unit was not started automatically. Start it manually from the Services tab once you're ready to test it - see the note above about testing standalone first.
install.phpmyadmin.description: phpMyAdmin (English-only build) for managing MariaDB/MySQL databases via the browser. Installs into /opt/caddy-dashboard/phpmyadmin with its own dedicated PHP-FPM pool on PHP 8.3 (the latest phpMyAdmin release doesn't support PHP 8.4). No database credentials are stored - you log in with your own real MariaDB/MySQL account through phpMyAdmin's own login form. Wiring it into Caddy is a manual step - the ready-to-paste config block is shown after install.
install.phpmyadmin.confirm_install: Install phpMyAdmin? This downloads the latest release and may take a minute.
phpmyadmin.requires_php83: Requires PHP 8.3 first - install it from the PHP-FPM tile (the latest phpMyAdmin release doesn't support PHP 8.4).
phpmyadmin.caddy_hint: Paste this into your Caddyfile (edit the domain) to make it reachable - this step is manual, the panel doesn't touch your live Caddy config.
phpmyadmin.confirm_uninstall: Remove phpMyAdmin? This deletes the files and the dedicated PHP-FPM pool (your databases are untouched).
install.adminer.description: Adminer (all-languages build, includes a Polish UI switch) - a single-file database tool covering MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MS SQL and Oracle out of the box - no need to install phpMyAdmin just to reach MariaDB. Installs into /opt/caddy-dashboard/adminer with its own dedicated PHP-FPM pool on PHP 8.3. A MongoDB plugin is downloaded automatically, but MongoDB won't actually work until you also enable the pecl-mongodb module for PHP 8.3 (Services -> PHP 8.3 -> PHP Modules) - that's a deliberate manual step, since PHP extensions are shared by the whole PHP-FPM service, not just Adminer. No database credentials are stored - you log in with your own real account through Adminer's own login form. Wiring it into Caddy is a manual step - the ready-to-paste config block is shown after install.
install.adminer.confirm_install: Install Adminer? This downloads the latest release and may take a minute.
adminer.requires_php83: Requires PHP 8.3 first - install it from the PHP-FPM tile.
adminer.caddy_hint: Paste this into your Caddyfile (edit the domain) to make it reachable - this step is manual, the panel doesn't touch your live Caddy config.
adminer.confirm_uninstall: Remove Adminer? This deletes the file and the dedicated PHP-FPM pool (your databases are untouched).
phpmyadmin.gate_description: Puts a Cloudflare Turnstile bot-check in front of phpMyAdmin's own login page, using the same keys as the panel's login (Services -> Caddy). This doesn't touch phpMyAdmin itself - it's a checkpoint at the Caddy layer, wired manually (paste the block below, replacing your current phpMyAdmin block). Off by default - a deliberate choice, not automatic just because phpMyAdmin is installed.
phpmyadmin.gate_requires_turnstile: Turnstile isn't configured/enabled on the panel yet - configure it first under Services -> Caddy before enabling this gate.
phpmyadmin.gate_caddy_hint: This is the whole phpMyAdmin section (edit the domain) - replace your current phpMyAdmin block with this entirely, don't add it alongside:
phpmyadmin.gate_confirm_enable: Enable the Turnstile gate for phpMyAdmin? Turning this on alone doesn't change anything yet - you still need to update the Caddy config (block below) and restart Caddy.
phpmyadmin.gate_step1: Enable it here in the panel (this toggle).
phpmyadmin.gate_step2: Update the Caddy config - paste the whole block below in place of the current phpMyAdmin block.
phpmyadmin.gate_step3: Restart Caddy: sudo systemctl reload caddy
phpmyadmin.gate_confirm_disable: Disable the Turnstile gate? phpMyAdmin will be reachable without the bot-check again (if the Caddy block is still in place, it'll just always let requests through).
adminer.gate_description: Puts a Cloudflare Turnstile bot-check in front of Adminer's own login page, using the same keys as the panel's login (Services -> Caddy). This doesn't touch Adminer itself - it's a checkpoint at the Caddy layer, wired manually (paste the block below, replacing your current Adminer block). Off by default - a deliberate choice, not automatic just because Adminer is installed.
adminer.gate_requires_turnstile: Turnstile isn't configured/enabled on the panel yet - configure it first under Services -> Caddy before enabling this gate.
adminer.gate_caddy_hint: This is the whole Adminer section (edit the domain) - replace your current Adminer block with this entirely, don't add it alongside:
adminer.gate_confirm_enable: Enable the Turnstile gate for Adminer? Turning this on alone doesn't change anything yet - you still need to update the Caddy config (block below) and restart Caddy.
adminer.gate_step1: Enable it here in the panel (this toggle).
adminer.gate_step2: Update the Caddy config - paste the whole block below in place of the current Adminer block.
adminer.gate_step3: Restart Caddy: sudo systemctl reload caddy
adminer.gate_confirm_disable: Disable the Turnstile gate? Adminer will be reachable without the bot-check again (if the Caddy block is still in place, it'll just always let requests through).
phpsettings.title: Settings
phpsettings.description: Basic settings for this PHP version. Changes reload the PHP-FPM service (no full restart) and apply to every site using this version.
phpsettings.timezone_hint: Used e.g. when an app doesn't set its own timezone explicitly
phpsettings.memory_limit_hint: How much RAM a single PHP process can use - too low causes 'Allowed memory size exhausted' errors
phpsettings.max_execution_time_hint: PHP kills a running script after this many seconds (e.g. a long data import)
phpsettings.max_input_time_hint: Time to receive and parse input data (form, upload) before the script itself starts
phpsettings.max_input_vars_hint: Too low breaks large forms (e.g. feature-rich shops, panels with many fields)
phpsettings.max_file_uploads_hint: How many files can be sent at once in a single request (e.g. a photo gallery upload)
phpsettings.expose_php_hint: Revealing the PHP version makes it easier for attackers to target exploits at that specific version - recommended off.
phpsettings.read_failed: Couldn't read the current PHP configuration - the values below are only proposed defaults, not the real state.
phpopcache.title: OPcache
phpopcache.description: PHP compiled-bytecode cache - key for performance. Changes reload PHP-FPM.
phpopcache.memory_hint: Memory reserved for the compiled-code cache - too little causes frequent cache resets and lower performance
phpopcache.interned_strings_hint: Buffer for shared strings - too small increases memory use from duplicates
phpopcache.max_files_hint: Should exceed the number of .php files across your projects, otherwise the cache won't fit them all
phpopcache.revalidate_freq_hint: How often OPcache checks whether a file on disk has changed
phpopcache.validate_timestamps_hint: Disabling gives the highest performance, but code changes then require a manual PHP-FPM reload
phpopcache.read_failed: Couldn't read the current OPcache configuration - the values below are only proposed defaults, not the real state.
phpopcache.confirm_save: Save the new OPcache settings? The PHP-FPM service will be reloaded.
